finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST 'feed' parameter is passed unvalidated to file_get_contents(), enabling SSRF (blind, with a response-length oracle) and file:// / ftp:// reads.
finding.source: $_POST['feed'] at import.php:11 (POST, no auth check on this branch)

trace.note: Branch taken on POST with isset($_POST['feed']); no require_admin() or session check.
Raw attacker-supplied URL passed to file_get_contents(); PHP stream wrappers (http, https, ftp, file) accepted by default.
Only strlen($xml) is echoed, so the fetch is blind but body length is leaked as an oracle.

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host/IP allowlist or private/link-local blocking, port restriction, redirect validation, authentication/authorization on this branch, or return-value/error check. The admin check at import.php:4-9 protects only the set_webhook branch and does not apply here.

verdict.reason: import.php:11 takes the POST branch on any request with $_POST['feed'] set and no auth check, and import.php:12 passes that raw value to file_get_contents() with no scheme, host, or port validation; the only admin check (require_admin(), import.php:4-9) is called solely from the set_webhook branch at line 18, and line 13 echoes strlen($xml), so the claimed blind SSRF with a length oracle is accurately described.
